?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:23734
Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 170 of 2024

Applicant :- Sushil Kumar Patel
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Hari Bans Singh,G.A.,G.A.,Hari Bans Singh
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri R.N. Srivastava, learned AGA for the State apprised the Court that he has received the instructions, therefore, instant anticipatory bail application may be finally disposed off.

2. Heard Sri Hari Bans Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.N. Srivastava, learned AGA for the State.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 143 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 313 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Meja, District Prayagraj with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail during trial.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was performed with the informant on 20.05.2020 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured the informant for dowry and on 05.02.2023 applicant assaulted the informant and due to the assault made by him she sustained serious injuries and on 06.02.2023 during treatment her miscarriage was caused.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and admittedly at the time of alleged miscarriage informant was not residing in her matrimonial home.

6. He further submits that some matrimonial dispute arose between husband and wife and thereafter informant herself left her matrimonial home and only dispute is that informant did not want to beget her second child and in spite of resistance shown by the applicant, she herself caused her miscarriage and subsequently after two months, she lodged FIR of the present case on the basis of false allegation.
7. He further submits that except the verbal allegation, there is no evidence that applicant caused miscarriage of the informant.
He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and investigation of the case is still pending and police is trying to arrest the applicant.

8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not dispute the fact that except the bald allegation, there is no evidence that applicant caused miscarriage to the informant.
He further could not dispute the fact that at the time of miscarriage informant was not residing in her matrimonial home.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Present dispute appears to be matrimonial dispute and applicant is husband of the informant and however as per allegation due to the injury caused by the applicant dated 05.02.2023 miscarriage of the informant was caused on 06.02.2023 but it appears that except the bald allegation, there is no such evidence that due to the injury caused by the applicant, her miscarriage was caused.

11. Further, even from the record, it reflects that at the time of miscarriage i.e. on 06.02.2023 informant was not in her matrimonial home and a day before, as per allegation, she was turned out from her matrimonial home.

Further, investigation of the case is still pending and police is trying to arrest the applicant.
12.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

16. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
